scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by laying out the facts as I understand them. I'm 18, and I have a twin sister. My best friend, G, and I have been friends since kindergarten. G and my sister have always been close, and they've had a sort of "thing" going on for a long time. They finally started dating when we were 17, and everything was great for about 13 months. Then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and told my sister, even though G begged me not to. We didn't talk for a month and a half, which was really weird for me because G is like my brother. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip to make amends. I went, and we talked things out. He cried, which I've only seen once before, and I forgave him. Now, G and my sister are broken up, and they're not speaking. My sister is upset with me for still being friends with G and doesn't understand why our 13-year friendship is so important to me. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it, but I don't want to lose our friendship over this. I'm planning to go to the same college as G in the fall, which is in a different state than where my sister is going. So, the question is: Am I being an asshole? Let me break this down. First, I need to consider the perspectives involved. There's my perspective, my sister's, and G's. I also need to think about the dynamics of the friendships and relationships involved. From my perspective, G is my best friend, someone I've known since kindergarten. We've been through a lot together, and losing that connection would be really hard. I forgave him because I saw that he was genuinely sorry, and I couldn't imagine life without him. I also think that if my best friend cheated on their SO, I wouldn't end the friendship. So, why should this situation be any different just because the SO is my sister? From my sister's perspective, she was cheated on by someone she was in a relationship with. She's hurt, and she's probably feeling betrayed. She might see G as someone who hurt her, and she doesn't understand why I can still be friends with him. She might feel that I'm prioritizing G's friendship over her feelings, which is why she's making me feel bad about it. From G's perspective, he made a mistake, he's sorry, and he's trying to make things right. He's reached out, apologized, and seems to have taken responsibility for his actions. He's also dealing with the fallout of the breakup with my sister. Now, considering all this, is it wrong for me to continue the friendship with G? Or am I being an asshole by not supporting my sister? I think it's important to consider the following points: 1. **Friendship vs. Relationship**: My friendship with G is separate from my sister's relationship with him. Just because G hurt my sister doesn't automatically mean I have to end our friendship. However, I need to be sensitive to my sister's feelings. 2. **Forgiveness**: I chose to forgive G, which is a personal decision. Forgiveness doesn't mean forgetting, but it does mean moving past the issue. However, my sister might not be ready to forgive, and that's her right. 3. **Supporting My Sister**: My sister is hurt, and she needs support. By continuing the friendship with G, I might be seen as not supporting her. I need to find a balance between maintaining my friendship and being there for my sister. 4. **Long-term Implications**: We're all moving on to college, which might naturally create some distance. The situation might become less of an issue as we're in different places. 5. **Communication**: I should communicate with my sister about why I value my friendship with G and try to understand her perspective. Maybe we can find a middle ground where I maintain the friendship but also support her. 6. **Boundaries**: I need to set boundaries if my sister is pressuring me to end the friendship. It's important to respect both my feelings and hers, but ultimately, I have to make decisions that are right for me. 7. **Guilt and Pressure**: I'm feeling guilty because my sister is upset, but I also don't want to lose a friendship that's been important to me. It's a tough spot to be in. In conclusion, I don't think I'm being an asshole for wanting to keep my friendship with G, especially since he's shown genuine remorse. However, I do need to be mindful of my sister's feelings and make sure I'm supporting her as well. It's a delicate balance, but as long as I'm honest with both of them and respectful of their feelings, I can navigate this situation.
